title: Microburst protection: adaptive KV-priority windowing and soft backpressure
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: In high-QPS environments we observe short, high-amplitude microbursts that defeat steady-state batching heuristics and cause KV cache churn, increased GPU memory pressure, and transient P95/P99 latency spikes. This ticket scopes an adaptive microburst defense that combines short sliding admission windows, KV priority tiers for cached prefixes, and a soft backpressure mechanism that paces admitted requests rather than rejecting them outright. Goals: 1) Reduce P99 tail during bursty windows by at least 25% relative to current baseline; 2) Reduce KV cache thrashing (measured by cache eviction rate) under bursts; 3) Avoid sudden GPU OOMs by bounding transient memory usage with soft reservations and prioritized eviction. Approach summary: - Introduce a short sliding microburst window (configurable 50-500ms) that tracks incoming request arrival-rate and recent batch formation latency. - Maintain KV priority tiers: HOT (recently used, strong affinity), WARM (mid recency), COLD (rare). Eviction and admission decisions favor HOT prefixes. - Implement probabilistic admission scoring: each incoming request receives an admission token based on window fill, prefix priority, and request importance signal (route/model). Admission is soft: low-score requests are paced (added to a local async queue with jitter) instead of being dropped. - Add a temporary GPU memory headroom reservation that scales with admitted token count to prevent immediate OOM during spike-driven batch joins. - Expose telemetry and knobs in the Console: microburst window size, admission aggressiveness, KV priority TTLs, memory headroom fraction. - Rollout as opt-in feature flag per-customer for 2-week canary before global default.
acceptance_criteria: Sustained burst benchmark (synthetic arrival pattern with 5x baseline QPS for 300ms every 5s): P99 latency reduced >= 25% compared to current master with same model and hardware
KV cache eviction rate during bursts reduced by >= 30% for HOT prefixes measured over 1M request trace
No increase in steady-state (non-burst) average latency > 1% when feature enabled
No GPU OOMs observed in canary runs across 50+ trials on dedicated cluster staging
Telemetry surfaces per-window admission rate, paced queue length, and memory headroom usage in Console dashboard
tasks: Design: finalize sliding-window math, admission scoring formula, and KV tier transitions (design doc linked)
Implement: admission controller in runtime request ingress path with pluggable scoring
Implement: KV priority annotation & tiered eviction hooks in kv-cache module
Implement: soft pacing queue and jittered retry policy per request
Implement: GPU memory headroom reservation and graceful fallback path
Instrument: metrics (admitted, paced, dropped, eviction_by_tier, headroom_usage, p99_by_window) and traces
Test: unit tests for scoring logic and KV-tier transitions
Benchmark: run synthetic microburst workload and record baselines (p50/p95/p99, throughput, eviction rate)
Canary: enable opt-in for 10 internal customers and run 2-week telemetry collection
Rollout: plan staged rollout, feature gate default, and rollback criteria
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive admission reduces immediate latency but can increase batch sizes and temporarily raise memory pressure — mitigated by headroom reservations and tiered eviction
We chose soft pacing over hard rejections to preserve developer experience for customer-facing requests; some internal low-priority traffic may be dropped under severe overload (configurable)
KV tiers reuse existing recency counters but add a small per-prefix score to avoid global TTL churn
Potential risk: inaccurate request importance signal could bias admission — plan to surface per-route logs and allow route-level overrides
Open question: default microburst window size across GPU types; propose profiling on A100 vs RTX6000 and recording recommended defaults in runtime-1.20 release notes
